profiles.name: Pedro Zenón Encarnacíon
profiles.description:
Pedro Zenón Encarnacíon crossed the line at Fort Benning, Georgia during an SOA Watch vigil to close the U.S. Army School of the Americas / WHINSEC. Sentenced to 3 months.

Each year on the November anniversary of the assassination of six Jesuits, their housekeeper, and her daughter at the University of Central America in San Salvador in 1989, peace activists gather at the gates of Fort Benning, Georgia, site of the U.S. Army School of the Americas / Western Hemisphere Institute for Security Cooperation (WHINSEC), to commemorate the dead and to call for the school's closure. Hundreds have crossed the line onto the base over four decades of vigils; many have served federal sentences ranging from 30 days to a year for trespass.
profiles.finding: Vieques court-case and BlackStar film leads found; no verified portrait. Existing SOA biography may conflate cases; review needed.

profiles.name: Aaron Labe Linas
profiles.description: Aaron Labe Linas, age 19, was convicted of conspiracy to damage and destroy property by means of fire and explosives in connection with ELF-claimed actions against suburban-development sites in Richmond, Virginia. Sentenced to 42 months federal prison plus 3 years supervised release and $204,021.86 in restitution.
profiles.finding: Government hearing confirms Richmond ELF case; no verified portrait.

profiles.name: Adam Blackwell
profiles.description:
Adam Virden Blackwell, age 20, was convicted of criminal conspiracy and aiding and abetting in connection with ELF-claimed planned actions against suburban-development sites in Richmond, Virginia. Sentenced to 60 months federal prison.

Blackwell and his co-defendants John Wade and Aaron Linas were Douglas S. Freeman High School students in Henrico County who had belonged to the school’s Friends of Earth Club before adopting Earth Liberation Front tactics. Between July and October 2002 the three set kerosene-soaked wicks in the fuel tanks of construction equipment at the Short Pump Town Center mall site, etched slogans into 25 SUVs at a dealership, and vandalized fast-food restaurants, leaving ELF graffiti. Blackwell pled guilty in federal court in Richmond on January 12, 2004.
profiles.finding: Saskatoon hockey player rejected; no verified Richmond ELF defendant portrait.

profiles.name: Nydia Gonzalez Reyes
profiles.description:
Nydia Gonzalez Reyes was arrested for trespass on the U.S. Navy bombing range at Vieques, Puerto Rico, as part of the sustained 1999–2003 civil-disobedience campaign that ultimately forced the Navy to withdraw from the inhabited island in May 2003. Sentenced to awaiting trial.

From 1941 to 2003, the U.S. Navy used the inhabited Puerto Rican island of Vieques as a live-fire bombing range. After Navy bombs killed civilian security guard David Sanes in 1999, a sustained civil-disobedience movement of Puerto Rican residents and U.S. solidarity activists repeatedly entered Navy land to halt training. Hundreds were arrested and dozens served federal prison sentences for trespass, conspiracy, and damage to federal property. The Navy finally withdrew from Vieques in May 2003 — the largest victory in U.S. anti-base activism in a generation.
profiles.finding: NotiCel legal-services union president and Vieques petition leads need custody identity confirmation.

profiles.name: Erik Johnson
profiles.description: Erik Johnson of Maryville, Tennessee crossed the line at Fort Benning, Georgia during the November 2001 SOA Watch vigil opposing the U.S. Army School of the Americas / WHINSEC. He was sentenced in July 2002 to six months in federal custody and served the term from September 10, 2002 to March 10, 2003 under BOP number 90971-020.
profiles.finding: Athletes, physician and education professionals lack link to Maryville SOA prisoner; rejected.

profiles.name: Joanna Cohen
profiles.description: Convicted in U.S. District Court for the Middle District of Georgia under 18 U.S.C. § 1382 (entering a military reservation) for participating in the School of the Americas Watch (SOA Watch) annual nonviolent civil-disobedience action at Fort Benning, Georgia on September 2002. The action targeted the U.S. Army Western Hemisphere Institute for Security Cooperation (WHINSEC) — formerly the School of the Americas — which had trained Latin American military officers later linked to assassinations, torture, and massacres including Romero, the four U.S. churchwomen, the Jesuits in El Salvador, El Mozote, and Plan Cóndor. Defendants typically received 3 to 6 months in federal custody plus a fine.
profiles.finding: Academic, lawyer and education advocate results not linked to SOA defendant.

profiles.description: Jim Cosner was arrested during a May 22, 2002 demonstration in Santa Cruz, California, opposing Representative Sam Farr’s support for the developing war in Iraq. Police charged Jim Cosner with resisting arrest. Contemporary follow-up reporting says Cosner later had an outstanding warrant after leaving the area, while Zerriffi was scheduled for trial on February 28, 2003. No accessible record establishes a jail booking, release time or final disposition.
